## Intent
Hypothesis: Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG can approach the streaming ceiling when paired with a simple render loop.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is FLAT across all N at every death rate. At q=0.01, cost drifts from 37.2 ns/p (N=10000) down to 36.2 ns/p (N=10000000) — a 2.7% decrease, not a rise. The L2 spill at N≈7710 is already crossed at the smallest measured point (N=10000), and the L3 spill at N≈246723 falls between N=100000 and N=1000000 with no visible knee. Death rate raises the floor without altering the N-shape: q=0.5 sits at ~40–41 ns/p versus ~36–37 at q=0.01, a ~10% penalty. There is no cache-saturation regime; cost is dominated by per-particle overhead, not memory hierarchy.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 1.88 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 14.8% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: bandwidth stays in a narrow 1.66–1.88 GB/s band across all N and death rates and never transitions toward the ceiling. Death rate erodes the peak modestly: q=0.5 peaks at 1.71 GB/s (13.5% of ceiling). The flat, sub-15% utilization at every regime confirms the bottleneck is frontend/compute overhead, not memory throughput.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize. The histogram shows zero vector-suffixed instructions; all floating-point work is scalar: `vmovss` (13), `vmulss` (4), `vaddss` (1), `vsubss` (1), `vucomiss` (8), `vcvttss2si` (5). There is no gather — particle data is accessed via scalar `vmovss` loads at fixed offsets from `rcx` (e.g., `vmovss xmm4,[rcx-0x8]`, `[rcx-0x4]`, `[rcx]`). The per-particle loop is branch-heavy: 24 `cmp`, 12 `cmovae`, 10 `jae`, 6 `jne`, plus `sets`/`setge`/`setle`/`setl` predicates. Scatter writes are byte-granular: `mov BYTE PTR [r13+r15*1+0x0],bl` repeated for each RGBA channel with `movzx`/`add`/`cmp`/`cmovae` clamping to 0xff. This scalar, branchy, byte-store codegen explains both the 59.9% frontend stall and the 14.8% bandwidth utilization — the frontend cannot feed enough useful work to saturate memory.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 1.88 GB/s (14.8% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate, and the compiler produced zero vector instructions. The 59.9% frontend stall and scalar byte-granular scatter stores confirm the Halide-expressible branchless blend did not translate into vectorized or streaming code; the hypothesis fails across all measured regimes.
